Tula was half asleep but Sofi seemed to think everything was fine and Janity seemed to be following Sofi’s lead. (Janity’s vital signs were mostly all right, though she looked numb and exhausted.) Naja was a little shaky as she stood up, and Three offered her its arm to steady her as she stepped on the mobility device. As we started walking again, I said on our secure team feed, Do not stop as we go through the dock entrance. If we have a problem, follow Three, it will take you to our shuttle. Three already knew how to handle weapons scanners so I sent it the code bundle I was using to alter the humans’ IDs. I could tell from Farai’s expression she wanted to ask questions, but she knew it was a bad time to do it. Three added, I hope you will be satisfied with my service— Don’t, I interrupted. You don’t have to say that. Oh, Three sent. Okay. It told the humans, I apologize, it’s in the buffer, sometimes it just comes out. Perfectly all right, Farai sent back, though I doubted she had any idea what that phrase meant or why I had stopped Three from saying it. Please don’t apologize. Sofi sent Three a dozen sparkly hug sigils. As we got closer to the private docks entrance, I watched our time counter and our progress on the map projection I had thrown together, superimposed on the feeds from the security cameras outside the public docks. We hit our first mark on the timeline and Three triggered the Distraction1 file, the false alarm on the public docks. There was no immediate reaction around us, we were too far away for a visual from that end of the port and the alarms were feed-restricted to port personnel. But ahead of us, the B-E group reacted, their body language turning agitated. One made a sharp motion indicating it wanted the others to shut up. They were listening to their comm, getting orders from whoever was in charge. But they weren’t leaving their post. Yeah, I mean, we knew they probably wouldn’t. Three was right about a distraction being an obvious tactic and they were too far from the public docks to be their supervisor’s first choice for backup. On our private connection, Three sent, Additional hostiles in play, and sent me a camera view. Shit. Another armed group had just come out of an admin access in a Port Authority booth barely twenty meters from the private docks entrance. I had marked that booth as a potential hiding spot for hostiles, which was why Three had it on its monitor list, but shit. There were five in armor in front, behind them a smaller group wearing Barish-Estranza executive livery. They weren’t running, they were walking, but they were turning toward us. They are going to head toward the public docks and fucking walk right past us and there is an 85+ percent chance that they will know what Janity and Tula look like. Three was in the middle of suggesting we trigger Distraction2 early when I triggered Distraction2. I was glad I had coded it in advance instead of winging it. I could do it fast, but having the file ready to load meant it happened even faster than that. For three full seconds I didn’t know if it had worked or not. Distraction2 was based on an assumption, that B-E had hired local security companies because the port would give them at least limited access, and that access would include the basic ID scans for entrances to any restricted spaces, particularly in the vicinity of the dock entrances. (The whole plan was also based on the assumption that if both distractions didn’t work, we would have a chance to abort and try again, but we hadn’t accounted for the reserve B-E group walking right toward us.) Then all the hostiles, the reserve group strolling this way and the main group at the private docks entrance, all reacted at once. The hostiles in B-E livery shouted at the armored hostiles and the reserve group turned away from our position. In orderly chaos, both groups ran toward the restricted VIP waiting area. What my code had done was substitute Janity and Tula’s original ID codes for two of the IDs the HuntSolas corporate group had used to get into the restricted waiting area. Holy shit, it worked. Yeah, I thought it would, that’s why I did it, but. Shit. On the team feed, I said, Walk faster . Naja said aloud, “Oh, we’re late. Come on, everybody.” Farai made shooing motions and the kids obligingly sped up. Then we were under the arches, past the scanning gate and into the docks. I felt a wave of emotion that made my organic skin prickle with sweat. It was relief. There was a scatter of humans and bots in this area, most heading to or away from the outer hullside, where there were six levels of locks reachable by different ramps. On the team feed, Janity said, Are we— Is it okay now— Farai threw a look at me and I guess I didn’t look as stressed anymore, because she told Janity, We’re almost there . Head for lock 219, I sent. Three had the docks map up and was already steering us in the right direction. We were within three meters of the entrance to the second-level ramp when from behind us, someone called out, “Janity!” I didn’t scream, though I considered it for .02 of a second. On the team feed, I sent, Keep going . But Janity stopped and turned around. So I did, too.
